QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_35

question.text: When a Social Impact Assessor engages a field-level research agency or subject-matter expert for a SAS 1100 slum-housing engagement, which of the following is TRUE under Section 5.11?

answer.text: The SIA's responsibility for the SIA report is transferred to the expert once engaged

The SIA remains primarily responsible for the SIA report; must evaluate the expert's competence, capabilities and objectivity; must agree the nature/scope/objectives in writing and should not refer to the expert in the report unless required by law or regulation
The SIA can refer to the expert's findings in the report without any evaluation of competence or objectivity
Experts cannot be engaged under the SAS framework

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.11 states: 'the social impact assessor is primarily responsible for the social impact assessment report – even though he/she may delegate some aspects of the assessment work to field level research agency or uses work performed by other social impact assessors and experts.' The SIA must evaluate expert competence/capabilities/objectivity, agree terms in writing (nature, scope, objectives, communication, NDA), and 'should not refer to the work of an expert in the SIA report unless required by law or regulation. If such reference is required, the SIA should indicate that the reference does not reduce the SIA's responsibility.' The Trap: A wrongly transfers responsibility. C skips mandatory evaluation. D forbids experts, which contradicts Section 5.11 entirely. Cross-Exam Context: NISM XV (RA) and ICAI SA 620 (Using the Work of an Expert) use the same principle for financial audit; XXIII applies identical rigour. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Use a standard 'SME engagement agreement' template covering role, scope, NDA, source-data access rights, and deliverable format — saves time and ensures you meet the Section 5.11 six-point written-agreement checklist.
